title: Establishing when and how sustained plate tectonics began

concept.text: The innovation would be a convincing reconstruction of when and how Earth developed a persistent, globally connected system of moving tectonic plates. It would distinguish evidence of local subduction-like activity, crustal recycling or mobile regions from evidence that these processes formed an enduring global network. Finding an early example of tectonic activity would therefore be one piece of the reconstruction, rather than sufficient evidence of the full transition.

Conceptual synthesis: the target is both historical and mechanistic—establishing the timing of the transition and explaining the physical conditions that made sustained plate motion possible. A successful reconstruction could identify a prolonged, geographically uneven transition rather than a single first date. It could use younger rocks as well as Hadean material, because evidence of persistence and global connectivity may come from a different interval than the earliest evidence of local activity.

significance.text: Significance assessment: resolving this transition would provide a fundamental account of how Earth's surface and interior became coupled through sustained plate motion. Establishing the timing and mechanism together could explain a major change in how the planet exchanges material and heat, while helping distinguish competing accounts of its geological development. This is the anticipated importance of the proposed achievement; the supplied evidence does not demonstrate that the reconstruction has been accomplished.

Conditional consequences: a well-supported tectonic history could constrain models of continental growth and long-term geochemical cycles by specifying when sustained recycling and plate interactions became available as explanatory mechanisms. Implications for the history of life or the behavior of other planets would require additional evidence and modeling. Establishing Earth's transition would not, by itself, establish a universal planetary sequence or a particular biological consequence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is to infer an enduring global tectonic regime from observations that are geographically scattered and potentially compatible with several histories. A local recycling signal might indicate isolated or intermittent activity without establishing a connected plate network. The reconstruction must therefore explain how individual observations constrain spatial connectivity, duration and the physical mechanism of sustained motion.

Research-framed barriers, not verified findings from the retained source: the supplied research identifies the scarcity of ancient rocks and alteration of potentially diagnostic signatures as major obstacles. Addressing these concerns would require reliable dating, checks that the relevant signatures survived later geological changes, and evidence that the proposed tectonic interpretation fits better than alternatives. The possibility of a gradual or regionally uneven transition must remain open; it is a hypothesis to evaluate rather than an established history in this record.

Proposed engineering and scientific requirement: physical models must connect plausible early-Earth conditions to the initiation and persistence of plate motion, while producing consequences that can be compared with geological observations. Matching one regional signal would be insufficient if the same model could not account for the broader distribution and timing of evidence. Conversely, an apparent mismatch must be assessed against the incompleteness and preservation limits of the geological archive.

current_state.text: The supplied research lists a 2026 study attributed to Valley, Blum, Kitajima and colleagues, titled “Contemporaneous mobile- and stagnant-lid tectonics on the Hadean Earth,” with DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-10066-2. The research reports that its abstract interprets zircon evidence as indicating contrasting tectonic histories in different regions. This makes the study potentially relevant to the distinction between regional mobility and a uniform global regime, but that scientific interpretation could not be independently checked in the supplied review.

The access records differ in a consequential way: the research says the abstract was inspected and full-text access failed, whereas the review found that the retained HTML contained only a cookie challenge. The retained material therefore did not allow the reviewer to verify article identity from its content, examine the abstract, or assess methods, results and limitations. The source index's saved and verified indicators do not resolve that absence of scientific content. This limits what can be concluded here; it is not evidence that the reported study or interpretation is false.

Assessment of the supplied evidence: no verified demonstration in this record establishes the onset date or mechanism of a sustained global plate network. Even if the reported regional zircon interpretation is confirmed, an additional argument would be needed to connect regional tectonic differences to global connectivity and long-term persistence. The review also reports an empty freshness-search record, so the supplied material cannot establish a comprehensive state of knowledge through its stated November 1, 2026 cutoff.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed convincing demonstration: assemble independently dated evidence from multiple regions, explain which observations diagnose local mobility and which constrain sustained connectivity, and test the interpretations against plausible alternatives. Preservation assessments should show why the relevant signals are attributable to the geological interval under study rather than later alteration. Independent corroboration should add distinct constraints rather than repeatedly rely on the same underlying observation.
completion_criteria.label: Independently dated regional evidence distinguishes local mobility from sustained connectivity

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: make the observations, dating uncertainties, interpretive assumptions and physical-model methods sufficiently available for independent groups to repeat the analyses and evaluate competing histories. A persuasive result would show how conclusions change when uncertain observations or model assumptions are varied, including whether the inferred transition remains supported when particular regions are excluded.
completion_criteria.label: Available evidence and methods enable independent reconstruction and robustness testing

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: completion need not mean identifying one exact onset date. A defensible interval or sequence of regional transitions could satisfy the goal if it explains how sustained global tectonics emerged and clearly distinguishes established findings from unresolved parts of the reconstruction. Evidence from a finite set of sites would establish the demonstrated geographic and temporal breadth of that account, rather than literal observation of every plate boundary or proof of uninterrupted behavior everywhere. These are proposed criteria, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Onset reconstruction explains sustained global tectonics within stated evidential limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based scope comparison: GEO-05, “Recovery of a detailed geological record of Earth’s first half-billion years,” is the closest overlap. Its title describes a broad early-Earth archive, whereas GEO-08 targets a specific tectonic transition and its mechanism, potentially using younger evidence as well. The full GEO-05 entry was not supplied, so its actual methods and overlap remain unverified. GEO-07, “Reconstructing the Moon-forming impact from independent geological evidence,” likewise concerns reconstruction of an ancient event, but addresses a different historical target; the supplied material does not establish a causal connection between the two.

Roster-based conceptual comparison: GEO-02, “A chemically and thermally resolved map of Earth’s deep interior,” could provide a complementary perspective on surface–interior coupling, but mapping internal structure and reconstructing tectonic onset are distinct goals. GEO-09, “Predictive laws linking erosion, sediment transport and landscape evolution,” concerns surface processes that may affect geological archives; predictive landscape laws would not independently establish when a global plate network began.

Roster-based practical comparison: GEO-01, “Reliable short-term forecasting of damaging earthquakes,” and GEO-10, “Reliable transferable forecasting of volcanic eruptions,” concern prediction of future hazards. GEO-03, “Geothermal reservoirs engineered economically in ordinary deep rock,” GEO-04, “Global-scale, verifiable mineral storage of carbon dioxide,” and GEO-06, “Discovery of globally consequential recoverable geological hydrogen,” concern energy or storage capabilities and resources. They share a broad geological setting with GEO-08, but resolving ancient tectonic onset would not by itself deliver their forecasting, engineering or resource objectives.

change_log.change: Preserved GEO-08's identity while expanding the distinction between local tectonic signals and a persistent global plate network.
change_log.reason: That distinction defines the scientific target and prevents an isolated early observation from being treated as proof of sustained global tectonics.

change_log.change: Recast the 2026 zircon interpretation as a finding reported by the supplied research that the review could not independently verify.
change_log.reason: The research reports abstract access, but the retained artifact available to the reviewer contained only a cookie challenge.

change_log.change: Preserved rock scarcity, alteration and a potentially uneven transition as research-framed concerns and hypotheses.
change_log.reason: The retained source does not substantiate these assertions, but the review did not contradict them or justify removing the concept.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to address alternative interpretations, reproducibility, uncertainty and geographic coverage.
change_log.reason: These requirements make the distinction between intermittent regional activity and sustained global tectonics assessable without demanding an exact onset date or literal universality.

change_log.change: Retained conditional geological significance and explicit limits on planetary and biological implications.
change_log.reason: The anticipated consequences are coherent assessments, but neither the achievement nor its downstream implications are demonstrated by the supplied evidence.

change_log.reason: The roster supports a title-level scope comparison, but the full GEO-05 entry was unavailable to verify actual overlap.

unresolved_issues: The discrepancy between reported abstract inspection and the cookie-only retained artifact remains unresolved; the scientific content and article identity cannot be independently verified from that artifact.
The zircon study's methods, quantitative results, preservation checks and interpretation remain unavailable for assessment in the supplied review.
The supplied material does not establish whether subsequent research resolves or changes the onset question; the freshness-search record is empty.
The actual scope and methods of GEO-05 require comparison with its full entry.
The diagnostic observations and temporal coverage sufficient to distinguish sustained global connectivity from intermittent regional mobility remain to be specified and justified.

brief.title: Knowing when and how Earth's moving plates began
possible: We could trace how the ground beneath us became part of a lasting, worldwide system of moving plates, called plate tectonics. A reconstruction would explain when that system took hold and what physical conditions kept it moving.
why: This would explain a major change in how Earth's surface and interior exchange heat and material. It would help geologists understand how continents grew and how long-term chemical cycles developed.

sources.who: John W. Valley, Tyler B. Blum, Kouki Kitajima and colleagues
sources.showed: Zircons, durable mineral crystals, carry chemical signs of contrasting regional histories on early Earth. The authors interpret some as evidence of subduction, where surface rock sinks into Earth's interior.
sources.quote: Subduction-related magmatism in the Hadean, as documented by JH zircons, alternated with periods of magmatic quiescence.
sources.cited_for: Different regions could have experienced different styles of movement during Earth's earliest era.
sources.not_established: Regional signs of sinking surface rock leave the timing and persistence of a connected global plate system unresolved.

sources.who: Jikai Ding, Chris Rogers, Ulf Söderlund and colleagues
sources.showed: Ancient magnetic directions preserved in rocks support relative sideways movement between the Wyoming and Superior continental blocks before about 2.5 billion years ago.
sources.quote: The results provide strong evidence for relative horizontal motion between crustal blocks during the Neoarchean.
sources.cited_for: Separate continental blocks moved relative to each other deep in Earth's past.
sources.not_established: Movement between these blocks leaves the origin and worldwide extent of a lasting plate network unresolved.

sources.who: Bo Huang, Tim E. Johnson, Simon A. Wilde and colleagues
sources.showed: Associated rocks in northern China record seafloor spreading and subduction operating in the same period. The authors argue that these preserve ancient plate-boundary processes.
sources.quote: These assemblages record seafloor spreading and contemporaneous subduction initiation and mature arc magmatism, respectively, analogous to modern divergent and convergent plate boundary processes.
sources.cited_for: A regional rock sequence links processes that create seafloor with processes that consume it.
sources.not_established: This regional history leaves global connectivity and the onset of sustained worldwide plate motion unresolved.

sources.who: Roger R. Fu, Nadja Drabon, Benjamin P. Weiss and colleagues
sources.showed: Their statistical reanalysis found that sparse measurements of ancient magnetic-field strength in zircons allow widely different histories of surface movement.
sources.quote: We conclude that Archean zircon paleointensities do not provide evidence for or against mobile-lid plate tectonics prior to 3.4 Ga.
sources.cited_for: Uncertainty in ancient magnetic measurements can prevent a reliable choice between competing movement histories.
sources.not_established: The analysis leaves early plate motion unresolved, and the original age of the crystals' magnetic signals remains disputed.

sources.who: Bradford J. Foley, David Bercovici and Linda T. Elkins-Tanton
sources.showed: In a preprint, physical models show how shrinking mineral grains could weaken Earth's outer shell enough for early subduction, followed by a transition as Earth cooled.
sources.quote:
After the initiation of proto-subduction, non-plate-tectonic
“sluggish subduction” prevails, giving way to modern style plate tectonics
as both the mantle interior and climate cool.
sources.cited_for: A physical mechanism could connect early sinking rock to the later development of plate motion.
sources.not_established: A modeled pathway still needs geological tests that establish when it operated and how it produced sustained global motion.

shown: Ding and colleagues found magnetic evidence that continental blocks moved relative to each other. Huang and colleagues linked ancient seafloor spreading and subduction in northern China. These results establish parts of the history needed to reconstruct a lasting global system.
missing: A reconstruction must connect scattered regional observations into evidence of a lasting worldwide plate network.
Ancient signals need reliable ages and evidence that later heating or alteration preserved their original meaning.
Physical models must explain the geographic pattern and timing of observations while accounting for gaps in surviving rocks.

milestones.label: Dated regional evidence establishes lasting connections
milestones.explanation: Independently dated observations across regions would have to establish local movement, lasting connections and preservation, while testing alternatives. This would connect regional clues to the wider system.

milestones.label: Independent groups reproduce and test the reconstruction
milestones.explanation: Independent groups would have to repeat analyses using accessible observations and methods, varying uncertain assumptions and excluding regions. This would establish how strongly the reconstruction depends on particular choices.

milestones.label: A reconstruction explains the emergence of sustained global motion
milestones.explanation: A reconstruction would have to explain how a lasting global system emerged, within the geographic and time span its evidence supports. An interval or regional sequence could establish when and how the transition unfolded.

uncertain: The transition may have unfolded gradually, with different regions changing at different times.
Which observations and time spans can establish lasting global connections remains an open question.
Several processes can produce similar chemical signatures in ancient crystals, complicating their interpretation.

page.title: Reconstruction of the onset of sustained global plate tectonics
page.definition: A reconstruction would identify when Earth's rigid outer shell became a sustained, globally connected system of moving plates and explain the physical transition. It would distinguish that system from isolated or intermittent subduction, in which surface rock sinks into the mantle.

goal.need: Published estimates place the onset of plate tectonics between 4.2 and 0.7 billion years ago. Resolving that range would constrain when sustained plate motion became available to explain exchange of heat and material between Earth's interior and surface. The National Academies identifies the timing and physical origin of plate tectonics as a science priority.

statements.body: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
statements.quote: When, why, and how did plate tectonics start?
statements.context: Science Priority Question 2 in A Vision for NSF Earth Sciences 2020–2030: Earth in Time.

statements.body: Geological Society of America Penrose Conference participants
statements.quote: answering the question of when plate tectonics began is critical for understanding the evolution of the solid earth system
statements.context: The conveners report this agreement among participants, while reporting disagreement over the onset and its geological indicators.

completion.title: A reconstruction dates and physically explains the onset of sustained global plate tectonics.
completion.criterion: A geological reconstruction constrains an onset interval or sequence for a sustained global network of rigid plates with coexisting seafloor spreading and subduction. A physical explanation accounts for its initiation and persistence under the inferred early-Earth conditions. The dated evidence discriminates this account from competing onset histories and episodic regional recycling. Regional subduction evidence or a simulation demonstrating physical possibility alone does not satisfy the test.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback, bounded by the National Academies' timing-and-origin question and published geological recognition criteria.
completion.basis: Searches of the National Academies' Earth in Time, GSA's Penrose report and geological/geodynamic reviews found no operational test combining onset timing, global persistence and mechanism. This fallback joins the published goal to the global-system criterion. Foley et al.'s arXiv manuscript models proto-subduction within about 100 million years of magma-ocean solidification, explicitly distinguishing it from modern plate tectonics.

milestones.title: Ancient continental blocks preserve geological evidence of rigid lithosphere.
milestones.criterion: Dated sedimentary basins on stable substrates or rectilinear swarms of tabular igneous intrusions, called dykes, provide geological evidence for rigid continental lithosphere. Cawood et al. identify extensive North Atlantic craton dyke emplacement at about 3.5 and 3.25 billion years ago.
milestones.set_by: Geological recognition convention summarized by Cawood et al. (2018), section 3, Evidence for rigid lithosphere.
milestones.threshold_quote: Rigid lithosphere is taken to be a necessary pre-condition for plate tectonics.

milestones.title: Paleomagnetic records demonstrate relative horizontal motion between at least two continental blocks.
milestones.criterion: Two or more continental blocks have different, coeval apparent polar wander paths: tracks of ancient magnetic-pole positions inferred from their rocks. Ding et al. sampled 26 Wyoming dykes; one dated dyke yielded 2,480 ± 4 million years. Their Wyoming–Superior comparison establishes relative motion between 2.71 and 2.48 billion years ago. Conversely, Fu et al.'s reanalysis of 91 zircon paleointensities permits all latitudinal displacements at 95% confidence between 3.408 and 3.908 billion years ago when the two source regions move independently.
milestones.set_by: Paleomagnetic relative-motion test stated by Ding et al. (2024), Introduction; it distinguishes differential block motion from common motion caused by true polar wander.
milestones.threshold_quote: requires differing paleomagnetic apparent polar wander paths between the blocks over the same time interval

milestones.title: Associated ancient rock assemblages demonstrate contemporaneous seafloor spreading and subduction.
milestones.criterion: Dated rock assemblages record spatially associated, contemporaneous seafloor spreading and subduction. Huang et al. interpret the Angou Complex, North China, as preserving these processes at 2.55–2.51 billion years ago, followed by arc–continent collision at 2.51–2.45 billion years ago. Their source-composition modelling uses 21 mid-ocean-ridge-type and six island-arc-type rock samples. This supports regional plate-boundary interaction.
milestones.set_by: Plate-boundary recognition convention stated and applied by Huang et al. (2022), Abstract and Introduction; their demonstration concerns the southern North China Craton.
milestones.threshold_quote: The coexistence of divergent (spreading ridge) and convergent (subduction zone) plate boundaries

milestones.title: A geological synthesis supports sustained interaction within a globally linked system of plate boundaries.
milestones.criterion: Geological evidence supports sustained, globally linked plate-boundary interaction. Cawood et al. infer a transition about 3.2–2.5 billion years ago, while acknowledging that pre-Pangaea global connectivity cannot be unequivocally proven. Valley et al., published on 4 February 2026, interpret Jack Hills and Barberton zircon chemistry as evidence for different contemporaneous regional regimes; these observations do not establish a persistent global network. This milestone concerns the geological reconstruction before its physical cause is resolved.
milestones.set_by: Global-system recognition criterion published by Cawood et al. (2018), Conclusion; a qualitative geological criterion, without an agreed numerical acceptance threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: sustained and part of a global system of plate boundary interaction.

not_found: No published minimum duration or geographic sampling requirement was found for identifying the onset of a sustained global plate network.
The publisher-hosted version of Foley et al. could not be opened; its manuscript on arXiv, marked accepted by Journal of Geophysical Research, was accessible.

results.finding: Jack Hills zircons older than 3.8 Ga: 71% of 249 had a continental-arc-like Sc/Yb signature.
results.detail: The comparison with Barberton supports different contemporaneous regional tectonic regimes, but does not establish sustained global connectivity. The text gives n=249 for the Jack Hills comparison, while Table 1 gives n=254.
results.quote:
In the JH suite, the proportion of >3.8 Ga zircons with Sc/Yb > 0.1 is four times greater (71%,
n
= 249) than in BGSB (18%) (Table
1
).

results.finding: Paleomagnetic analysis of 26 Wyoming dykes and comparison with Superior indicate relative motion between 2.71 and 2.48 Ga.
results.detail: Thirteen dykes contributed to the new Wyoming pole; comparison with Superior's coeval poles constrains the relative motion.
results.quote: The present study documents Neoarchean relative lateral motion between cratons on the order of thousands of km, demonstrably between 2.71 and 2.48 Ga, and likely occurring prior to 2.63 Ga.

results.finding: A synthesis spanning 11 cratons reports an aggregate continuity of convergence records through 2.8–2.5 Ga.
results.detail: Continuity in aggregate convergence records challenges prolonged global quiescence but does not establish sustained interaction in a globally connected plate-boundary network.
results.quote: such models predict global-scale tectonic quiescence on the order of ca. 100 million years between the putative overturn events that are contradicted by a continuity of aggregate records for convergence through the 2.8–2.5 Ga interval

results.finding: Angou Complex assemblages record spreading and subduction at 2.55–2.51 Ga; source modeling used 21 ridge-type and 6 arc-type samples.
results.detail: The reconstruction supports regional plate-boundary interaction; the ridge and subduction interpretations combine field, geochemical and modeling evidence.
results.quote: Here, we document temporally- and spatially-associated Neoarchean (2.55–2.51 Ga) rock assemblages with mid-ocean ridge and supra-subduction-zone origins from the Angou Complex, southern North China Craton.

results.finding: Reanalysis of 91 zircon paleointensities permits all latitudinal displacements at 95% confidence.
results.detail: For separately analyzed Jack Hills and Green Sandstone Bed source regions over 3.408–3.908 Ga, the data do not demonstrate relative horizontal motion or establish apparent polar wander paths. The analysis assumes the zircon signals are primary, which the authors note is disputed.
results.quote:
We find that, in the 3.408 to 3.908 Ga interval, any amount of 
latitudinal motion is permissible within the 95 % confidence intervals 
implied by the data.

results.finding: Ameralik dykes, North Atlantic craton: sample size not reported; dated to 3.5 and 3.25 billion years ago.
results.detail: The paper identifies the Ameralik and equivalent Saglek dykes as extensive intrusions cutting stable continental crust.

results.finding: Paleomagnetic comparison of East Pilbara and Barberton: sample size not reported; differential motion at approximately 3.48 Ga.
results.detail: The source reports differential motion between the blocks, but does not state whether their coeval apparent polar wander paths differ.
results.quote: We present paleomagnetic data quantifying differential motion between lithospheric blocks at ~3.48 billion years ago (Ga).

results.finding: Seismic evidence from six continents supports a linked global subduction network by ~2 billion years ago.
results.detail: The synthesis links inferred sutures during Nuna’s assembly; some continental positions and extensions of sutures remain uncertain.
results.quote:
Seismic evidence of subduction from six continents at this age is interpreted 
as the oldest evidence of global plate tectonics. The sutures identified can be linked in a plate network that resulted 
in the assembly of Nuna, likely Earth’s first supercontinent.

results.finding: Global plate reconstruction using 209 paleomagnetic poles extends from 1.8 billion years ago to the present.
results.detail: The geological and geophysical synthesis supports sustained plate interaction across the reconstructed period. Pre-Pangean oceanic plates and some boundaries are inferred or synthetic, and the authors present the model as a working hypothesis.
results.quote:
Here, we present a new full-plate tectonic reconstruction from 1.8 Ga to present that combines
and reﬁnes three published models: one full-plate tectonic model spanning 1 Ga to present and two
continental-drift models focused on the late Paleoproterozoic to Mesoproterozoic eras.
